chunks: Mansour ibn al-Abbas, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Zari' al-Basri, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
We mentioned the olives in his presence, so the man said, 'It brings the wind.' He said: 'No, but it dispels the wind.'
ai.seo_question: What is the effect of olives on wind according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Imam’s precision in distinguishing between the humoral properties of olives, correcting the common misconception that they attract wind (a reference to the 'wind' element or phlegm in traditional medicine) by affirming their ability to repel it. This aligns with Shia scholarly tradition which views the Prophet’s family as possessing deep knowledge of both spiritual and physical sciences, including the medicinal benefits of foods mentioned in the Quran. The statement underscores the practical wisdom embedded in the Imams' teachings, guiding believers toward health and well-being through accurate understanding of creation.

en.hubeali:
Mansour Bin Al Abbas, from Ibrahim Bin Muhammad al Zara’a Al Basry, from a man, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,
‘We mentioned the Olives in his<sup>asws</sup> presence, so the man said, ‘It brings the wind’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, but it dispels the wind’.
en.sarwar: 5. Mansur ibn al-‘Abbas has narrated from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Zari‘ al-Basriy from a man who has said the following: “We mentioned olives before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and a man said it stirs up gas. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, it dispels gas.’”
